cells.tense: The practice is running here without any need to force it.
cells.act: let one structure collapse that could not hold
cells.ask: Let one way you have been working at this fall away if it can't hold, and don't pick it back up.
cells.core:
The practice carries itself now, which means you can feel when an hour actually matters and when it is only filling time. You've stopped treating every effort as equal, and the quiet that once felt isolating is where the good work comes from. That is why the details refine you instead of wearing you down: you know which of them are worth the hour.

Something in how you work won't survive the next honest look. Let it go when you see it. A routine, a habit of checking, a story about how this has to go — if it can't hold, stop holding it up and watch it come down. What is real stays. What was false opens room for the next stretch, and you can stand in that room a while without rushing to fill it.
cells.sheetLine: Let what you've been propping up fall and see what's left.
cells.verb: practise until the small thing is true in the hands
cells.place: where you can tell what matters before you can put it into words

cells.tense: Every session from here is being rehearsed before it is even started.
cells.act: put it down and leave your hands empty a while
cells.ask: After the next session, put the work down on purpose and leave the rest of the evening empty.
cells.core:
The practice is running ahead of you. You are already inside tomorrow's session before today's is finished, and the refining has stopped being a craft and started being a way to keep something bad from arriving. The isolation feels necessary now instead of chosen, and the hours get longer while the relief gets shorter.

Finish the next session and then set it down on purpose. Not because you've earned it, and not as a reward. Put it down the way you put down a tool when the work is done, and leave your hands empty for an evening. Nothing collapses when you stop gripping. The practice is still there in the morning, and the part of you that fears stopping gets to see it doesn't have to be feared.

cells.tense: The practice was once set down and the ground it stood on still feels unsafe.
cells.act: trade one thing for one thing, and keep no score
cells.ask: Do one short session and trade it for one equal rest, with no debt and no score kept.
cells.core:
You can see what matters here, and you still don't come to the practice. Something about it was made to feel costly, and the body has kept the bill. What is missing is the plain sense that effort and return can be exchanged evenly, without one side owing the other.

Make one small session and swap it for one real rest, on the spot, with nothing carried over. You give the time; you get it back in something you can feel. No debt, no making up, no proving. The point is not to rebuild the practice this week. The point is to make one fair trade and let your body learn the exchange can close.

cells.tense: The expertise has arrived and you still say you are only keeping your hand in.
cells.act: dream it from what you have already lived
cells.ask: Sketch where this practice goes next using only what you've already lived through, and keep it rough.
cells.core:
People ask how you got good at this and you say it just happened. The practice is real and you are not in the account of it. You can tell what matters here long before you can put it into words, and the way you describe it leaves that out. The skill arrived, and the one who kept showing up does not get named.

Start from what you have already lived. Take one page and sketch where this goes next using only the hours you have already put in — the changes you can feel in your hands, the things you now notice first. Scratchy is fine. Seeing it on the page is how the claim comes back. You are not guessing at a future; you are reading one off what you already did.
cells.sheetLine: Sketch where this goes next from the hours already behind you.
cells.verb: practise until the small thing is true in the hands
cells.place: where you can tell what matters before you can put it into words

attempts.check: The record does not support saying what past experiences made practice feel dangerous, so the Too Little core stays on the present fact of the door and does not name what happened. A reader could say the Too Little ask is just doing the practice, but the act is a fair exchange of effort and rest, not a push into the empty seat, and it survives if the read is wrong. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person is 'the door is behind you; nothing is there to walk back to'; the served line would rather tell them what is gone than let them stand where they are.
